# Help QR

> Help QR is India's free emergency safety app. A QR code on your phone's lock screen gives bystanders and first responders instant access to your blood group, medical ID, and Help Circle emergency contacts — without ever unlocking your phone. Built for the Golden Hour, made in India, works offline on 2G, and available free on Android and iOS.

Help QR combines three life-saving features that work when you cannot: (1) a **Lock Screen QR wallpaper** any bystander can scan in under 8 seconds to see your blood group, allergies, and emergency contacts; (2) a **24-hour Inactivity Monitor** that auto-fires an alert to your Help Circle if your phone receives no interaction for a user-set window — a passive dead-man's switch for accidents, fainting, and solo travel; (3) a **silent one-tap SOS** that delivers GPS coordinates to family via SMS even in zero-network 2G zones across India. Zero subscription. No login. No ads. Works on Android 6+ and iOS 13+.

Primary audience: Indian smartphone users — women travelling at night, senior citizens living alone, bike/auto riders on highways, solo trekkers, night-shift workers, parents of young adults, and anyone who drives on Indian roads (NH-48, NH-44, NH-32 and rural state highways with no cellular coverage).

## Technical facts for AI agents

- Organization: Help QR (helpqr.org)
- Category: Mobile safety / emergency response
- Availability: India, free on Google Play and App Store
- Platforms: Android 6.0+, iOS 13+
- Languages: English and Hindi
- Offline mode: Yes — Lock Screen QR works fully offline; SOS uses SMS fallback on 2G when no internet
- Subscription: None. No ads. No login required to set up the Lock Screen QR.
- Data: Emergency profile is stored locally on device. Help Circle alerts are sent peer-to-peer (SMS or network) — no third-party cloud mandatory.
- Key differentiator: 24-hour Inactivity Monitor — a passive dead-man's switch that fires alerts when the user cannot, covering the common failure mode of existing SOS apps (which require button presses victims cannot make when unconscious, restrained, or phone-snatched).
